claims.text: A Pulumi blog post titled "SST Runs on the Pulumi Engine: What It Means to Build on Pulumi" exists at /blog/sst-built-on-pulumi/.
AWS CDK ties infrastructure to AWS, and multi-cloud is nearly impossible with CDK.
AWS CDK supports defining infrastructure only in TypeScript or Python.
Pulumi supports AWS, Azure, GCP, and on-prem; AWS CDK is AWS-only.
Pulumi deployments are faster than AWS CDK because of direct execution versus CloudFormation.
AWS CDK supports only AWS Secrets Manager for secrets management, while Pulumi supports cross-cloud secrets.
AWS CDK uses a CloudFormation state file while Pulumi uses Pulumi-managed state.
Ion is the code name for SST's new deployment engine that deploys components using Pulumi instead of CDK and CloudFormation, and once stable will be released as SST v3.
SST uses Pulumi for its providers and deployment engine and bridges Terraform providers through Pulumi.
SST makes money primarily through its managed service SST Console, which is optional and has a free tier.
Pulumi lets you define infrastructure in TypeScript, Python, Go, or C# and deploy across AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, and on-premises.

SST's Founding Engineer said: "With Pulumi, the deployment process feels like a natural extension of writing code - it's intuitive and powerful and capable of advanced things that traditional IaC tools can't handle."
Pulumi Crosswalk for AWS is described in the AWS guide at /docs/iac/guides/clouds/aws/.
SST v3 replaced AWS CDK and CloudFormation with an embedded Pulumi engine that calls Terraform-bridged providers to make cloud API calls.
Running `sst deploy` needs no separate Pulumi install and no Pulumi account; the engine ships inside the SST CLI, with state kept in an S3 bucket in the user's own AWS account.
SST is an open source TypeScript framework from the team formerly known as Serverless Stack, for deploying to AWS and more than 150 other providers.
Through 2023 SST's provisioning layer was built on AWS CDK and CloudFormation; in late 2023 the team began a rewrite code-named Ion.
Ion shipped as SST v3 in mid-2024 and has been the only supported architecture since.

SST's blog post 'Moving away from CDK' says: "Ion is a code name for a new engine for deploying SST applications. The constructs (or components) are defined using Terraform providers and deployed using Pulumi; as opposed to CDK and CloudFormation (CFN)."
SST's blog post 'Moving away from CDK' says that on `sst deploy`, resources call an embedded Pulumi engine that calls the bridged Terraform provider, which makes AWS SDK calls.
SST docs 'What is SST' say: "SST uses Pulumi behind the scenes for the providers and the deployment engine. And Terraform's providers are bridged through Pulumi."
Gautier Blandin's article says SST uses the Pulumi engine under the hood and lets users write Pulumi code in addition to SST constructs.
Kiryl Anoshka's dev.to article says: "You may notice right away the imports from Pulumi. It means the whole deployment process will be built on Pulumi now."

SST's platform package.json depends on @pulumi/pulumi, first-party Pulumi providers for AWS, Cloudflare, Docker builds, and a Pulumiverse Vercel provider, in the anomalyco/sst repository (formerly sst/sst).
Pulumi's Terraform bridge (pulumi-terraform-bridge) is Apache-2.0 licensed.
Pulumi's engine does not require a Pulumi account, network call to Pulumi Cloud, or any Pulumi-hosted service to run.
Pulumi's Automation API works for teams embedding Pulumi programs inside their own tools.
AWS alone exposes hundreds of resource types.
Nitric's docs state "all of the direct deployment providers use Pulumi under the hood for their deployments," with official Nitric providers built on Pulumi's AWS, GCP, and Azure providers.
Defang's pulumi-defang provider takes a Compose file, translates it to a Pulumi program, and runs `pulumi up`.
Resources without a dedicated SST construct can be defined directly in Pulumi and deployed as part of the same SST app.
The latest SST release, v4.17.1, went out in July 2026.
The `sst` npm package had roughly 796,000 (796,291) weekly downloads for September 5-11, 2026.
SST's team page credits the same team behind opencode, an open source AI coding agent.
opencode has a larger GitHub following (stars) than SST itself.
SST doesn't invoke the Terraform CLI or write Terraform state.
The opencode work hasn't changed SST's release cadence.
Pulumi's Terraform bridge lets any Pulumi user consume Terraform providers directly.
Pulumi Cloud, policy as code, and components are available Pulumi capabilities requiring no leaving of the engine.
